summary: Yasumi Matsuno's Ogre Battle saga, covering the real-time army tactics games, the Tactics Ogre branch, handheld side stories, and the modern Reborn remaster route.

entries.title: Ogre Battle: The March of the Black Queen

emulation.notes: Use an accurate PlayStation emulator, clean scaling, and standard disc-read settings.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PlayStation CD-era output with emulator scaling.

primary.why: The PlayStation port is a CD-era enhanced route with official English availability; Saturn and mobile releases are Japan-only routes and Virtual Console versions are convenience rereleases of the older game.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PlayStation version on original hardware or a PlayStation emulator with clean integer/upscaled output; use the Super NES version only if prioritizing the original cartridge release.

entries.remaster_caveats: Virtual Console and mobile releases are availability routes, not remasters.

entries.title: Tactics Ogre: Let Us Cling Together

emulation.notes: No emulation needed for the primary route; emulate Super Famicom, Saturn, PlayStation, or PSP only for historical comparison.

primary.why: Reborn is the modern remaster of the PSP remake, released on Windows and current consoles with improved graphics and sound, revised mechanics, and full English/Japanese voice acting; Windows is the most capture-friendly high-fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Tactics Ogre: Reborn on Windows/Steam at native display resolution; keep the original Super Famicom/PlayStation/Saturn releases as historical comparison material.

entries.remaster_caveats: Reborn changes battle mechanics and game balance; archive the 1995 and PSP releases as historical versions if comparing systems.

entries.title: Ogre Battle 64: Person of Lordly Caliber

emulation.notes: Use accurate plugins/settings first, then increase internal resolution if stable.

primary.why: Ogre Battle 64 is an N64 game with later Virtual Console rereleases of the same version; accurate N64 emulation gives the cleanest high-resolution capture route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Nintendo 64 version through a mature N64 emulator such as RMG, Project64, or Mupen64Plus with conservative accuracy settings and upscaled output.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster; Virtual Console releases are rereleases.

entries.title: Ogre Battle Gaiden: Prince of Zenobia

emulation.emulator: ares, Mednafen, or SameBoy-compatible NGPC core
emulation.notes: Use NGPC emulation or original hardware capture; verify language needs before streaming.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Neo Geo Pocket Color handheld output with emulator scaling.

primary.version: Japan-only Neo Geo Pocket Color release
primary.why: This side story was released only for Neo Geo Pocket Color in Japan; no official localized or remastered version is documented.
primary.how_to_play: Play on original Neo Geo Pocket Color hardware or an accurate NGPC emulator; for English commentary, prepare translation/context notes separately because the official release is Japan-only.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official remaster or localization documented.

entries.title: Tactics Ogre: The Knight of Lodis

emulation.notes: Use mGBA or hardware capture with clean scaling and color correction as preferred.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Game Boy Advance output with emulator scaling.

primary.why: The Knight of Lodis is documented as a Game Boy Advance title and no higher-fidelity official remake is documented.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Game Boy Advance release on original hardware with capture, Analogue Pocket, MiSTer, or a high-quality GBA emulator such as mGBA with integer scaling.
